data.note: Exclude always-run guards from the suite-slot count; admit selected runs on measured seconds and the computed worker count; fall back to file count. Globs narrowed to the files really written.

evidence.note: CLAIM: recorded ci gates can predict a selected run's wall time well enough to decide the suite slot; no per-test durations are stored (git grep: only pytest --durations as an ignored flag), but each ci gate records elapsed_s, waited_s, ci_scope.selected/always_s/ran/workers. MECHANISM: rate = (elapsed - waited - always_s) * workers / selected files; predicted = median(rate) * files / WK.compute(cfg, files).n, so load enters through the one governor. FALSIFIER: a per-run rate predicts no better than a constant, or a small unloaded run still predicts heavy. PROBE 1 (backtest of 200 recorded selected runs with a worker count, each predicted from up to 200 earlier ones, median/p90 relative error): constant 0.35/2.18, global rate 0.29/1.19, per-file attribution 0.28/1.11. Per-file is no better, so the global rate is used. PROBE 2 (real code on the real log: 6059 ci events, 200 measured, newest 50 median 184.2 worker-s/file, scan 0.6 ms; 192 cores): load/core 0.05: 3f 184s, 55f 211s, 100f 384s stay off the slot, 178f 683s takes it; 0.6: 55f 362s, 78f 513s stay, 100f 658s takes it; 0.75 and over: n=1, 3f 552s stays, 24f+ takes it. Falsifier not met. Default 600 s: selected wall p90 531 s, recorded full suite about 2000 s.

ddflow brief --item fix-Bc07bf8feb4, ddflow recall 'suite lock selected run admission'; read D-gate-economy-r3, D-agent-test-etiquette, L-load-governor-needs-auto (via lesson search), rule show r-upgrade-safe, r-bounded-everything, r-everything-configurable, r-derive-dont-store. Applied: rates are derived from the ci gate events, no new store (r-derive-dont-store); three new [ci] knobs with upgrade notes (r-everything-configurable, r-upgrade-safe); scan stops at selected_lock_runs (r-bounded-everything); load enters through workers.compute, the one governor (D-agent-test-etiquette); the selected ci gate and the test selection are untouched (D-gate-economy-r3).

Test first: tests/test_ci_suite_slot_cost.py and the changed boundary test ran on unfixed code: 20 failed, 10 passed, including test_a_few_files_plus_every_guard_do_not_need_the_suite_slot (assert True is False). Fixed head 79ce7a37e: 30 passed. New ddflow/services/ci/admission.py; runner._needs_suite_slot delegates to it and takes rates; cirun passes rates from the log; Plan.admission recorded in gate evidence with basis measured|file_count|off. Old test decision: default 20 stays (it is the fallback, now over the reached files only), the two assertions that counted guards were rewritten.

data.summary: ci.selected_lock_tests keeps default 20 but stops counting always-run guards. knob_changed would print 'default 20 -> 20' and feature says 'new opt-in feature', so neither is true; the change had to ride in the why of a sibling knob_added note. A kind such as knob_semantics_changed (key, why, effect, no old/new) is missing from upgrade_manifest.KINDS.
data.title: Upgrade manifest has no note kind for a knob whose meaning changed but whose default did not
